citations.name: requirements.sdk.graph.execution.deterministic_procedures
citations.commentary:
A criterion can also compute its answer with deterministic Rust code.
Its `ValidationContext` exposes the [inspection operations](context-tools.md)
used by the agent's graph tools.
[Searches and outlines](context-tools.md#find-a-node-then-read-its-contents)
help locate code to inspect; tracked reads and edge selections record input
identities and fingerprints, so changes to those inputs can invalidate the
resulting evidence.

{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.shared_context`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.search_text.behavior`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.outline_source.behavior`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs`
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`

rationale:
The passage is book commentary, and each of its claims is supported by the cited declarations.

- **Deterministic execution.** `requirements.sdk.graph.execution.deterministic_procedures` says a criterion can compute its answer directly from tracked inputs without a configured agent. That matches "A criterion can also compute its answer with deterministic Rust code".
- **Shared inspection context.** `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.shared_context` says `ValidationContext::inspection()` exposes the execution's `InspectionContext`. It also says `ToolAgent` delegates its graph-node reads, edge queries, and delivery recording to that same context. So "exposes the inspection operations used by the agent's graph tools" is supported.
- **Search and outline.** `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.search_text.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.outline_source.behavior` describe the search and outline commands. The commentary only says these help locate code to inspect. It doesn't claim they are tracked or that `ValidationContext` exposes them. The "Find a node, then read its contents" section of `context-tools.md` backs the discover-then-read flow it links to. That section's `search_text.inputs` and `outline_source.inputs` requirements say search and outline results record no inputs, and that a later tracked read does. The passage's wording agrees with this.
- **Evidence invalidation.** `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs` says `Fingerprinted` records node-content and successor-set observations. `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records` says `check_inputs` compares those fingerprints with current state. Together they support "tracked reads and edge selections record input identities and fingerprints, so changes to those inputs can invalidate the resulting evidence".

All six citations are `cite` role, which suits explanatory prose. The passage has no `impl` or `test` reference to the same requirements, so none is redundant.

text: :::{req} deterministic_procedures
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent. Evidence storage is still required.
:::{req} shared_context
```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
/// Borrow the inspection context shared by this criterion's operations.
pub fn inspection(&self) -> &InspectionContext<'d, D>;
`ValidationContext::inspection()` exposes the execution's `InspectionContext`.
The ask builder passes that context to `Agent::run`. The supplied `ToolAgent`
implements graph-node reads, outgoing-edge queries, and delivery recording by
delegating to that same context's operations.
Borrowing the context does not record an input. The reads and edge selections
performed through it contribute the observations described below.
:::{req} search_text.behavior
The supplied `SourceTools` adapter exposes `search_text` with a regular
expression and optional scope prefix, context-window size, and match limit.
These correspond to `TextQuery`'s `pattern`, `scope`, `context_lines`, and
`limit`. It uses `SourceProvider::search_text` and returns each match's
resource identity, line number, and excerpt, together with whether the search
is complete, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.search_completeness`.
:::{req} outline_source.behavior
The supplied `SourceTools` adapter exposes `outline_source` with a resource
identity. It parses that resource through `SourceAnalysis` and returns its
items' selectors and kinds. The Rust result is a `ParsedSource` containing
the resource identity, source bytes, and `Outline`; the tool presents the
outline's selectors and kinds.
:::{req} inputs
```rust,ignore
// Defined in habeas_sdk::graph.
/// A completed answer and the inputs used to produce it.
pub struct Fingerprinted<D: Domain, O> { /* private fields */ }
impl<D: Domain, O> Fingerprinted<D, O> {
/// The source node this answer concerns.
pub fn source_node_id(&self) -> &D::NodeId;
/// The question's path relative to that source.
pub fn criterion_path(&self) -> &CriterionPath;
/// The review rules used to produce this answer.
pub fn revision(&self) -> &str;
/// Recorded node-content and successor-set observations.
pub fn dependencies(&self) -> &[Dependency<D::NodeId, D::EdgeLabel>];
/// Borrow the completed answer.
pub fn output(&self) -> &O;
/// Take ownership of the completed answer.
pub fn into_output(self) -> O;
`verify` constructs this value from the criterion's completed answer and
execution trace. `load_evidence` reconstructs it from the selected saved record.
Its node identities and edge labels keep their domain-defined types.
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
// Method on Validator<D>.
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<O>(
&self,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The method resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
It uses the current state that the caller intends to inspect, rather than
reusing source snapshots from an earlier invocation without establishing that
they remain current. These reads are separate from a criterion execution's
dependency trace.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from execution. Reads used
only to check old evidence do not become dependencies of the new result. A
checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state; when
execution explicitly reads or delivers it, its fingerprint enters the new trace.
